# Adjudication Task — Chapter 701

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃701화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|“내 사냥개란다. 아주 공들여 길들인.”
  6|
  7|나직하게 울려 퍼지는 남천마후의 목소리. 그와 동시에 복면인이 걸음을 내디뎠다.
  8|
  9|저벅.
 10|
 11|뿌옇게 내려앉은 먼지구름 사이, 나아가는 걸음에는 한 치의 흔들림도 느껴지지 않는다.
 12|
 13|서서히 또렷해지는 복면인의 모습을 확인한 나는 신음처럼 중얼거렸다.
 14|
 15|“……시발. 저건 또 뭐야.”
 16|
 17|대답을 듣고자 흘린 말이 아니다. 나는 이미 이 의문에 대한 답을 알고 있으니까.
 18|
 19|재생(再生).
 20|
 21|그 두 글자로 지금 이 순간에도 눈앞에서 펼쳐지고 있는 저 기이한 광경을 설명할 수 있었다.
 22|
 23|으득, 스르륵.
 24|
 25|조각난 뼈가 붙고, 살과 피가 차오른다.
 26|
 27|마치 살아 있는 뱀처럼 구불거리는 어둠이 복면인의 전신을 스쳐 지나갈 때마다 상처가 회복되고, 새로운 힘이 스며들고 있었다.
 28|
 29|- 역천(逆天)의 힘…….
 30|
 31|역천.
 32|
 33|하늘의 뜻을, 순리를 역행하는 듯한 광경.
 34|
 35|수호령이 한탄과 같은 의념을 흘린 그때, 회복을 끝마친 복면인이 기이하게 뒤틀린 팔꿈치를 꺾었다.
 36|
 37|우두둑.
 38|
 39|이미 붙어 버린 팔꿈치를 스스로 부수고, 위치를 맞춰 다시 회복한다.
 40|
 41|엄청난 고통을 수반하는 행위임에도 눈썹 하나 까딱하지 않는 복면인의 모습에, 나는 전투 도중 느꼈던 위화감의 정체를 깨달았다.
 42|
 43|‘저놈은, 고통을 느끼지 못한다.’
 44|
 45|아무리 통각(痛覺)이 무딘 사람이라도 최소한의 고통은 느끼기 마련이다.
 46|
 47|하지만 복면인은 단 한 번도 신음이나 비명을 지르지 않았다.
 48|
 49|가슴에 비수가 박히고 팔꿈치가 으스러질 때도. 끔찍한 열기를 머금은 화염신장에 적중당했을 때도 마찬가지였다.
 50|
 51|‘도대체 무슨 짓을 한 거지?’
 52|
 53|어디서 무통 주사라도 맞고 왔나.
 54|
 55|복면 위로 드러난 무감정한 눈동자를 바라보며 침음성을 삼킨 그때, 새하얗고 자그마한 누군가의 발이 축축한 흙을 밟았다.
 56|
 57|사박.
 58|
 59|하늘에서 땅으로. 마침내 지면 위에 사뿐히 내려앉은 남천마후가 싱긋 웃었다.
 60|
 61|“귀신이라도 본 얼굴이네. 아니, 사실 그리 놀라진 않았겠구나? 하남에서 한 번 본 적이 있으니까.”
 62|
 63|크르르.
 64|
 65|낮은 울음소리와 함께, 군데군데 피로 얼룩진 거대한 동체가 지친 몸을 일으킨다.
 66|
 67|그러나 처음과는 확연한 차이가 있는 거친 호흡. 지금 당장 맞붙는다면 필패다.
 68|
 69|나는 수호령의 앞을 막아서며 입을 열었다.
 70|
 71|“그래, 혈주(血主). 그 미친 새끼도 마찬가지였지.”
 72|
 73|“아쉽네. 그때 혈주를 만나지 않았다면 지금쯤 기절초풍하는 네 모습을 볼 수 있었을 텐데.”
 74|
 75|“그 정도로 담이 작았으면 진작 뒈졌지.”
 76|
 77|“어려서 그런가? 허세는 어쩔 수가 없네.”
 78|
 79|허세라.
 80|
 81|소림혈사 당시 혈주가 보여 준 모습은 분명 놀라웠지만, 기절초풍할 정도는 아니었다.
 82|
 83|그러기에는 지금껏 내가 나고 자란 현대에서 보고 겪은 것이 너무나도 많다.
 84|
 85|“좋을 대로 생각하든지.”
 86|
 87|담담한 대답에서 무언가를 느낀 남천마후가 미간을 좁힌다.
 88|
 89|가늘어진 눈으로 나를 위아래로 훑어보던 그녀가 붉은 입술을 혀로 핥았다.
 90|
 91|“단순히 간이 큰 건지. 아니면 아무도 모르는 무언가가 있는 건지는 모르겠지만…… 역시 묘하단 말이야. 왜 천주께서 네게 흥미를 보이시는지, 조금은 알 것 같기도 해.”
 92|
 93|“관심?”
 94|
 95|되물은 나는 남천마후가 눈치채지 못할 만큼, 아주 천천히 공력을 순환시켰다.
 96|
 97|남천마후라는 괴물로도 벅찬데, 어디서 무통 주사를 처맞고 온 약쟁이까지 더해졌다. 조금이라도 앞서 입은 내상을 회복시키며 시간을 벌어야 한다.
 98|
 99|“그렇지 않아도 대설귀, 그 늙은이도 그런 헛소리를 지껄이긴 했지.”
100|
101|“어머. 그럼 혹시 지금도 헛소리라고 생각해?”
102|
103|남천마후가 싱긋 웃으며 한 걸음을 내디딘다. 나는 창대를 움켜쥔 손에 힘을 더하며 대답했다.
104|
105|“헛소리였으면 하는 바람이지.”
106|
107|“어째서?”
108|
109|“천주고 나발이고, 그런 정신 나간 늙은이한테는 관심받기 싫으니까. 지금 눈앞에 보이는 어느 미친년도 포함해서.”
110|
111|쉭, 피핏!
112|
113|아릿한 통증과 함께, 뺨이 뜨겁게 달아오른다. 간발의 차로 지풍(指風)을 피해 낸 내 모습에 남천마후가 안도의 한숨을 내쉬었다.
114|
115|“휴. 하마터면 죽일 뻔했네. 잘 피했어. 생각했던 것 이상인데?”
116|
117|이런 상황에서, 그것도 적에게 칭찬이라니.
118|
119|기분이 더러웠지만, 덕분에 두 가지 사실을 알았다.
120|
121|첫째. 저 괴물 같은 년이 전력을 다하더라도, 조금 전처럼 최소한의 피해를 입는다면 감당할 수 있다는 것.
122|
123|둘째. 나를 죽이면, 남천마후에게도 득보다 실이 크리라는 것.
124|
125|주르륵.
126|
127|나는 뺨을 타고 흐르는 피를 닦는 대신, 창대를 움켜쥔 손에 힘을 더하며 대꾸했다.
128|
129|“천주. 그 늙은이가 생각보다 나한테 관심이 많나 보네. 너 같은 미친년도 날 죽일까 봐 걱정하는 모습을 보면.”
130|
131|“……!”
132|
133|“이제야 대충 알 것 같아. 왜 호북성에서 나를 지켜만 봤었는지.”
134|
135|남천마후는 실로 강대한 무위를 지녔다. 내가 지금껏 보고 겪은 이들을 떠올려봐도, 그녀와 대적할 수 있을거라 여겨지는 사람은 극소수였다.
136|
137|‘낮게 잡아도 십왕(十王). 그 이상.’
138|
139|단지 마주하고 있는 것만으로도 느껴지는 거대한 힘.
140|
141|십왕 중에서도 논외로 취급받는 적천강을 제외한다면, 남천마후는 작금의 천하를 통틀어 최소 열 손가락 안에 드는 강자일 것이다.
142|
143|‘그런데도 아무 일도 없었지. 호북성에서 수십, 수백 번이나 손을 쓸 기회가 있었음에도.’
144|
145|남천마후의 정체를 깨달았을 때부터 줄곧 마음 속에 품고 있던 의문이다.
146|
147|왜 나를 살려 둔 걸까.
148|
149|죽일 가치조차 없어서? 단순한 유희로?
150|
151|비록 자세한 내막은 모르겠지만, 아니라는 확신이 들었다. 나는 다른 누구도 아닌 화왕(火王) 적천강의 하나뿐인 제자이자, 열화문의 후인이다.
152|
153|나를 수중에 넣는다면 향후 암천의 행보에 큰 걸림돌이 될 적천강을 끌어들여 해치울 수도 있고, 그 시도가 헛물을 켜도 열화문의 신공절학을 손에 넣을 수 있다.
154|
155|굳게 닫혀 있는 입을 벌릴 방법이야 많다.
156|
157|고문. 고문. 그리고 끊임없는 고문.
158|
159|하지만 남천마후는 자신에게 감쪽같이 속아 넘어간 나를 죽이지도, 그렇다고 납치하지도 않았다.
160|
161|그저 눈앞에서 지켜보다 홀연히 사라졌을 뿐이다. 마치 누군가의 명을 받고 찾아온 감시자처럼.
162|
163|나는 바싹 마른 입술을 달싹였다.
164|
165|“천주가 도대체 왜, 무슨 이유로 이렇게까지 내게 흥미를 보이는 거지? 나보다 더 관심을 둘 만한 이들이 있는데도.”
166|
167|그러나 내 물음에도, 언제부터인가 굳게 다물린 남천마후의 입술은 열리지 않았다.
168|
169|잠깐의 침묵 끝에 짧은 대답을 내뱉었을 뿐이었다.
170|
171|“너 따위 하찮은 존재가 뭘 알겠느냐. 전능하시고 지엄하신 그분의 뜻을.”
172|
173|하찮은 존재라.
174|
175|내심 중얼거린 나는 경직된 남천마후의 얼굴을 바라보았다.
176|
177|착 가라앉은 시선와 지그시 입술을 깨무는 모습 역시 놓치지 않았다.
178|
179|동시에 뇌리를 스친 한 줄기의 생각이 목소리가 되어 입 밖으로 흘러나왔다.
180|
181|“너, 모르지?”
182|
183|“……!”
184|
185|똑똑히 봤다. 순간 세차게 흔들리는 남천마후의 눈빛을. 그와 함께 비웃음 섞인 실소가 터져 나왔다.
186|
187|“병신.”
188|
189|“……뭐?”
190|
191|“병신이라고 했다. 이 하찮고 병신 같은 할망구야.”
192|
193|그리고 그 한 마디가, 남천마후라는 폭탄의 심지에 불을 붙였다.
194|
195|콰아아아아!
196|
197|막대한 기의 폭풍이 사방을 휩쓴다.
198|
199|전신에 새카만 어둠을 겹겹이 두른 남천마후의 모습에, 거친 숨을 가다듬은 수호령이 의념을 흘려보냈다.
200|
201|- 기왕 할 거, 조금만 더 시간을 끌지 그랬나.
202|
203|안 그래도 약간의 후회가 들었지만, 다른 방법이 없었다.
204|
205|내궁에 남아 있는 인간과 맹수들이 변이(變異)를 끝마치기 전에 결말을 지어야 한다. 이 중 누가 쓰러지고, 누가 서 있느냐는 그다음의 이야기다.
206|
207|나는 아직 성치 않은 몸으로 툴툴거리는 수호령을 향해 전음을 날렸다.
208|
209|- 수호령 맞냐? 곧 쓰러질 것처럼 빌빌거리지 말고 죽을 힘을 다해서 싸워.
210|
211|- 감히 날 모욕하다니. 삼백 년 전이었으면 인간 따위에게 이런 수모를 당하지도 않았을 것이다.
212|
213|- 그랬겠지. 그땐 저 미친년도 안 태어났을 테니까.
214|
215|- ……제기랄.
216|
217|수호령이라는 이름에 어울리지 않게 상스러운 말을 내뱉은 수호령이 전신의 털을 바싹 곤두세운다.
218|
219|앞뒤로 다가오는 두 인영을 스치듯 훑은 녀석이 중얼거렸다.
220|
221|- 상황이 더 어려워졌군.
222|
223|- 와. 난 진짜 전혀 몰랐던 사실인데, 역시 수호령이라 그런지 대단하네. 알려 줘서 고맙다.
224|
225|- 각자 하나씩 맡지. 인간 수컷과 인간 암컷. 둘 중 하나를 선택해라.
226|
227|- 그럼 내가 수컷.
228|
229|- …….
230|
231|이 새끼 양심 상태가?
232|
233|나를 빤히 바라보는 청백색 눈동자가 그렇게 묻는 듯했다. 개 같은 상황 속에서도 피식, 실소를 흘린 나는 걸음을 옮겼다.
234|
235|남천마후를 향해.
236|
237|저벅.
238|
239|긴장했기 때문일까.
240|
241|발걸음 소리가 유난히도 크게 울려 퍼진다. 어느새 피처럼 붉어진 안광(眼光)에 가슴 한구석이 서늘해졌다.
242|
243|“날 상대하겠다고? 너 따위가?”
244|
245|스산한 목소리. 나는 한숨을 푹 내쉬며 대답했다.
246|
247|“섭섭하네. 같은 하찮은 존재끼리 돕고 살아야지. 안 그래?”
248|
249|“……!”
250|
251|“선택해. 날 죽이고 천주한테 조인트 까이든지. 아니면 지금 여기서 곱게 뒈지든지.”
252|
253|카악, 퉤.
254|
255|죽은 피가 섞인 가래침을 탁 뱉은 나는 창날을 곧추세웠다.
256|
257|평소와는 다른, 낯설 만큼 차가운 목소리가 입술을 비집고 흘러 나온다.
258|
259|“참고로 난…… 죽을 때까지 싸운다.”
260|
261|화륵, 파앙!
262|
263|염화일로(炎火一路). 공기를 살라먹으며 쏘아지는 한 줄기의 화염.
264|
265|그리고 그 길의 끝에, 짙은 어둠을 두른 괴물이 있었다.
266|
267|쐐애애액, 꽈앙!
268|
269|
270|
271|* * *
272|
273|
274|
275|쾅!
276|
277|엄청난 충격파와 함께 세상이 뒤흔들렸다.
278|
279|진태경이 내리그은 창날에 지면이 갈라지고 끔찍한 열기가 터져 나온다.
280|
281|털끝 하나 차이로 일격을 피해 낸 남천마후가 손을 뻗었다.
282|

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

“Because I don’t want some deranged old man’s attention, Lord of Heaven or not. Same goes for the crazy bitch standing in front of me.”

[P53]
Whoosh—pfft!

[P54]
Pain stung my cheek, and heat spread across it. I’d dodged the Finger Qi by a hair.

[P55]
The Southern Heaven Demon Empress sighed in relief.

[P56]
“Phew. I nearly killed you. Good dodge. You’re better than I thought.”

[P57]
Praise from an enemy, at a time like this.

[P58]
It pissed me off. It also told me two things.

[P59]
First, even if that monster went all out, I could handle her attacks if I kept the damage as slight as I had just now.

[P60]
Second, she had more to lose than gain by killing me.

[P61]
Blood ran down my cheek. Instead of wiping it away, I tightened my grip on the spear.

[P62]
“The Lord of Heaven must be more interested in me than I thought. Even a crazy bitch like you is worried about killing me.”

[P63]
“…!”

[P64]
“I think I’m starting to understand why you only watched me in Hubei Province.”

[P65]
The Southern Heaven Demon Empress was staggeringly powerful. Of everyone I’d ever encountered, very few could stand against her.

[P66]
*At least on the level of the Ten Kings. Maybe higher.*

[P67]
I could feel the sheer force of her power just standing here.

[P68]
Apart from Jeok Cheongang, who was an exception even among the Ten Kings, she had to be one of the ten strongest people alive.

[P69]
*And yet she did nothing. She had dozens—hundreds—of chances to make a move in Hubei Province.*

[P70]
The question had stayed with me ever since I learned who she was.

[P71]
Why had she left me alive?

[P72]
Was I not worth killing? Was it all just a game to her?

[P73]
I didn’t know the full story, but I was certain neither answer was right. I was Fire King Jeok Cheongang’s only Disciple and a successor of the Fire Gate Clan.

[P74]
If she took me captive, she could use me to draw in Jeok Cheongang and kill him before he became a serious obstacle to Dark Heaven. Even if that failed, she could still get her hands on the Fire Gate Clan’s supreme martial arts.

[P75]
There were plenty of ways to make a man talk.

[P76]
Torture. Torture. And more torture.

[P77]
But she hadn’t killed me when I was completely taken in by her. She hadn’t abducted me either.

[P78]
She had simply watched me up close, then vanished. Like someone sent to keep an eye on me.

[P79]
My dry lips parted.

[P80]
“Why is the Lord of Heaven so interested in me? Why go this far when there are people far more worth his attention?”

[P81]
The Southern Heaven Demon Empress’s lips had pressed shut at some point. My question did nothing to open them.

[P82]
After a brief silence, she gave me a curt answer.

[P83]
“What could an insignificant creature like you know of that omnipotent, exalted one’s will?”

[P84]
*Insignificant.*

[P85]
I studied her tense face, the way her gaze had dropped and how she pressed her teeth lightly against her lip.

[P86]
A thought flashed through my mind. I spoke it aloud.

[P87]
“You don’t know, do you?”

[P88]
“…!”

[P89]
I saw her eyes waver. A derisive laugh slipped out of me.

[P90]
“Idiot.”

[P91]
“…What?”

[P92]
“I said you’re an idiot. You insignificant old hag.”

[P93]
That was enough to light the Southern Heaven Demon Empress’s fuse.

[P94]
Rooooar!

[P95]
A storm of qi swept out in every direction. Layer upon layer of pitch-black darkness wrapped around her.

[P96]
Beside me, the guardian spirit steadied its ragged breathing and sent me a thought.

[P97]
—If you were going to provoke her, couldn’t you have stalled a little longer?

[P98]
I regretted it a little myself. But there was no other way.

[P99]
We had to finish this before the humans and beasts still in the Inner Palace completed their mutation. Which of us fell and which remained standing came after that.

[P100]
I sent a Sound Transmission to the guardian spirit. It was still grumbling, though it was hardly in fighting shape itself.

[P101]
—Are you really a guardian spirit? Stop acting like you’re about to keel over and fight with everything you’ve got.

[P102]
—How dare you insult me. Three hundred years ago, I would never have endured such humiliation from a mere human.

[P103]
—Sure. That crazy bitch wouldn’t have been born yet, either.

[P104]
—…Damn it.

[P105]
Cursing in a manner hardly befitting a guardian spirit, it bristled from head to tail. Its gaze flicked over the two figures approaching us from front and back.

[P106]
—This has become more difficult.

[P107]
—Wow. I had absolutely no idea. Good thing you’re a guardian spirit. Thanks for telling me.

[P108]
—We’ll take one each. The human male or the human female. Choose.

[P109]
—Then I’ll take the male.

[P110]
—…

[P111]
*Does this bastard have no conscience?*

[P112]
That seemed to be what its pale blue eyes were asking me. Even in this godforsaken mess, I let out a short laugh and started walking.

[P113]
Toward the Southern Heaven Demon Empress.

[P114]
Step.

[P115]
Maybe it was nerves, but my footstep sounded unusually loud. Her eyes had turned blood red, and a chill ran through me.

[P116]
“You mean to fight me? You?”

[P117]
Her voice was cold. I let out a long sigh.

[P118]
“That hurts. We insignificant creatures ought to look out for each other. Don’t you think?”

[P119]
“…!”

[P120]
“Choose. Kill me and get your knees kicked in by the Lord of Heaven, or die quietly right here.”

[P121]
Hack—ptoo.

[P122]
I spat out a mouthful of phlegm mixed with stale blood and raised my spearhead.

[P123]
When I spoke again, my voice sounded unfamiliar. Cold.

[P124]
“For the record… I’ll fight until I die.”

[P125]
Fwoosh—bang!

[P126]
Flamefire Path.

[P127]
A single line of flame shot forward, consuming the air in its path.

[P128]
And at the end of that path stood a monster wrapped in darkness.

[P129]
Whoooosh—boom!

[P130]
* * *

[P131]
Bang!

[P132]
An immense shockwave shook the world.

[P133]
The ground split beneath Jin Taekyung’s descending spearhead, and searing heat burst from the fissure.

[P134]
The Southern Heaven Demon Empress dodged the strike by a hair and thrust out her hand.

[P135]
Rooooar!

[P136]
Her palm strike, charged with power beyond anything she had known before, met the spearhead streaking through the air like a ray of light.

[P137]
Qi collided with qi. The difference in strength was unmistakable.

[P138]
Boom!

[P139]
Compressed air exploded, and one figure was hurled backward.

[P140]
Delight shone in the Southern Heaven Demon Empress’s eyes.

[P141]
*He’s nothing.*

[P142]
Jin Taekyung’s martial arts had advanced at an unbelievable pace. He had changed so much that she could scarcely believe he was the same young man she’d met in Hubei.

[P143]
Perhaps the greatest obstacle to their grand plan was no longer the Beast Miao King, but Jin Taekyung.

[P144]
But…

[P145]
*I’ve grown stronger still.*

[P146]
She could feel power unlike anything she had known boiling through her body.

[P147]
The denser the demonic qi flowing from the rift grew, the stronger she became.

[P148]
Even now.

[P149]
Flash!

[P150]
One step.

[P151]
She vanished like a ghost and reappeared in midair.

[P152]
As she plunged toward him like a meteor, Jin Taekyung opened his eyes wide. He was still buried deep in the ground.

[P153]
Crunch.

[P154]
Solid earth crumbled like mud beneath her strike. Jin Taekyung escaped it by a hair and flicked his sleeve.

[P155]
A dagger flew at her from somewhere, as though he had conjured it from thin air. She avoided it easily and thrust out her hand with lightning speed.

[P156]
Slash!

[P157]
Her fingers only grazed him.

[P158]
But curled like hooks, they tore through his martial uniform and cut into his thigh.

[P159]
Blood spurted. Jin Taekyung staggered.

[P160]
The Southern Heaven Demon Empress beamed as she brought the edge of her hand down toward him.

[P161]
Whoooosh!

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

Crack. Rustle.

[P12]
Shattered bones joined together. Flesh and blood filled the wounds.

[P13]

—The power of defying heaven…

*Defying heaven.*

[P16]

[P17]

[P18]
Crunch.

[P21]
*That bastard can’t feel pain.*

[P23]

[P24]
*What the hell did they do to him?*

[P25]
Had he gone somewhere for a painkilling shot?

[P26]

[P27]
Softly.

[P28]

[P29]
“You look like you’ve seen a ghost. Then again, I suppose you aren’t that surprised. You saw something like this once in Henan.”

[P30]
Grrr.

[P31]
With a low growl, the guardian spirit raised its enormous, bloodstained body on weary limbs.

[P32]

[P33]
I stepped in front of it.

[P34]
“Yeah. The Blood Lord. That crazy bastard was the same.”

[P35]
“What a shame. If you hadn’t met the Blood Lord, I could’ve seen you scared out of your wits.”

[P36]
“If I scared that easily, I’d have died ages ago.”

[P37]
“Is it because you’re young? You just can’t help showing off.”

[P38]
*Showing off.*

[P39]
What the Blood Lord had done during the Shaolin Bloodshed had certainly surprised me. It hadn’t scared me out of my wits.

[P40]
I’d seen and been through too much in the modern world where I was born and raised.

[P41]
“Think whatever you want.”

[P42]
Something in my calm reply made the Southern Heaven Demon Empress draw her brows together. She looked me up and down through narrowed eyes, then licked her red lips.

[P43]
“I can’t tell if you’re simply brave or if you have something no one else knows about… But there’s something strange about you. I’m beginning to see why the Lord of Heaven takes an interest in you.”

[P44]
“An interest?”

[P45]
I began circulating my internal energy, slowly enough that she wouldn’t notice.

[P46]

[P47]
“The Great Snow Fiend spouted that same nonsense.”

[P48]
“Oh? Do you still think it’s nonsense?”

[P49]

[P50]
“I wish it were.”

[P51]
“Why?”

[P52]
“Because I don’t want some deranged old man’s attention, Lord of Heaven or not. Same goes for the crazy bitch standing in front of me.”

[P53]
Whoosh—pfft!

[P54]
Pain stung my cheek, and heat spread across it. I’d dodged the Finger Qi by a hair.

[P55]
The Southern Heaven Demon Empress sighed in relief.

[P56]
“Phew. I nearly killed you. Good dodge. You’re better than I thought.”

[P57]
Praise from an enemy, at a time like this.

[P58]
It pissed me off. It also told me two things.

[P59]
First, even if that monster went all out, I could handle her attacks if I kept the damage as slight as I had just now.

[P60]
Second, she had more to lose than gain by killing me.

[P61]
Blood ran down my cheek. Instead of wiping it away, I tightened my grip on the spear.

[P62]
“The Lord of Heaven must be more interested in me than I thought. Even a crazy bitch like you is worried about killing me.”

[P63]
“…!”

[P64]
“I think I’m starting to understand why you only watched me in Hubei Province.”

[P65]
The Southern Heaven Demon Empress was staggeringly powerful. Of everyone I’d ever encountered, very few could stand against her.

[P66]
*At least on the level of the Ten Kings. Maybe higher.*

[P67]
I could feel the sheer force of her power just standing here.

[P68]
Apart from Jeok Cheongang, who was an exception even among the Ten Kings, she had to be one of the ten strongest people alive.

[P69]
*And yet she did nothing. She had dozens—hundreds—of chances to make a move in Hubei Province.*

[P70]
The question had stayed with me ever since I learned who she was.

[P71]
Why had she left me alive?

[P72]
Was I not worth killing? Was it all just a game to her?

[P73]
I didn’t know the full story, but I was certain neither answer was right. I was Fire King Jeok Cheongang’s only Disciple and a successor of the Fire Gate Clan.

[P74]
If she took me captive, she could use me to draw in Jeok Cheongang and kill him before he became a serious obstacle to Dark Heaven. Even if that failed, she could still get her hands on the Fire Gate Clan’s supreme martial arts.

[P75]
There were plenty of ways to make a man talk.

[P76]
Torture. Torture. And more torture.

[P77]
But she hadn’t killed me when I was completely taken in by her. She hadn’t abducted me either.

[P78]
She had simply watched me up close, then vanished. Like someone sent to keep an eye on me.

[P79]
My dry lips parted.

[P80]
“Why is the Lord of Heaven so interested in me? Why go this far when there are people far more worth his attention?”

[P81]
The Southern Heaven Demon Empress’s lips had pressed shut at some point. My question did nothing to open them.

[P82]
After a brief silence, she gave me a curt answer.

[P83]
“What could an insignificant creature like you know of that omnipotent, exalted one’s will?”

[P84]
*Insignificant.*

[P85]
I studied her tense face, the way her gaze had dropped and how she pressed her teeth lightly against her lip.

[P86]
A thought flashed through my mind. I spoke it aloud.

[P87]
“You don’t know, do you?”

[P88]
“…!”

[P89]
I saw her eyes waver. A derisive laugh slipped out of me.

[P90]
“Idiot.”

[P91]
“…What?”

[P92]
“I said you’re an idiot. You insignificant old hag.”

[P93]
That was enough to light the Southern Heaven Demon Empress’s fuse.

[P94]
Rooooar!

[P95]
A storm of qi swept out in every direction. Layer upon layer of pitch-black darkness wrapped around her.

[P96]
Beside me, the guardian spirit steadied its ragged breathing and sent me a thought.

[P97]
—If you were going to provoke her, couldn’t you have stalled a little longer?

[P98]
I regretted it a little myself. But there was no other way.

[P99]
We had to finish this before the humans and beasts still in the Inner Palace completed their mutation. Which of us fell and which remained standing came after that.

[P100]
I sent a Sound Transmission to the guardian spirit. It was still grumbling, though it was hardly in fighting shape itself.

[P101]
—Are you really a guardian spirit? Stop acting like you’re about to keel over and fight with everything you’ve got.

[P102]
—How dare you insult me. Three hundred years ago, I would never have endured such humiliation from a mere human.

[P103]
—Sure. That crazy bitch wouldn’t have been born yet, either.

[P104]
—…Damn it.

[P105]
Cursing in a manner hardly befitting a guardian spirit, it bristled from head to tail. Its gaze flicked over the two figures approaching us from front and back.

[P106]
—This has become more difficult.

[P107]
—Wow. I had absolutely no idea. Good thing you’re a guardian spirit. Thanks for telling me.

[P108]
—We’ll take one each. The human male or the human female. Choose.

[P109]
—Then I’ll take the male.

[P110]
—…

[P111]
*Does this bastard have no conscience?*

[P112]
That seemed to be what its pale blue eyes were asking me. Even in this godforsaken mess, I let out a short laugh and started walking.

[P113]
Toward the Southern Heaven Demon Empress.

[P114]
Step.

[P115]
Maybe it was nerves, but my footstep sounded unusually loud. Her eyes had turned blood red, and a chill ran through me.

[P116]
“You mean to fight me? You?”

[P117]
Her voice was cold. I let out a long sigh.

[P118]
“That hurts. We insignificant creatures ought to look out for each other. Don’t you think?”

[P119]
“…!”

[P120]
“Choose. Kill me and get your knees kicked in by the Lord of Heaven, or die quietly right here.”

[P121]
Hack—ptoo.

[P122]
I spat out a mouthful of phlegm mixed with stale blood and raised my spearhead.

[P123]
When I spoke again, my voice sounded unfamiliar. Cold.

[P124]
“For the record… I’ll fight until I die.”

[P125]
Fwoosh—bang!

[P126]
Flamefire Path.

[P127]
A single line of flame shot forward, consuming the air in its path.

[P128]
And at the end of that path stood a monster wrapped in darkness.

[P129]
Whoooosh—boom!

[P130]
* * *

[P131]
Bang!

[P132]
An immense shockwave shook the world.

[P133]
The ground split beneath Jin Taekyung’s descending spearhead, and searing heat burst from the fissure.

[P134]
The Southern Heaven Demon Empress dodged the strike by a hair and thrust out her hand.

[P135]
Rooooar!

[P136]
Her palm strike, charged with power beyond anything she had known before, met the spearhead streaking through the air like a ray of light.

[P137]
Qi collided with qi. The difference in strength was unmistakable.

[P138]
Boom!

[P139]
Compressed air exploded, and one figure was hurled backward.

[P140]
Delight shone in the Southern Heaven Demon Empress’s eyes.

[P141]
*He’s nothing.*

[P142]
Jin Taekyung’s martial arts had advanced at an unbelievable pace. He had changed so much that she could scarcely believe he was the same young man she’d met in Hubei.

[P143]
Perhaps the greatest obstacle to their grand plan was no longer the Beast Miao King, but Jin Taekyung.

[P144]
But…

[P145]
*I’ve grown stronger still.*

[P146]
She could feel power unlike anything she had known boiling through her body.

[P147]
The denser the demonic qi flowing from the rift grew, the stronger she became.

[P148]
Even now.

[P149]
Flash!

[P150]
One step.

[P151]
She vanished like a ghost and reappeared in midair.

[P152]
As she plunged toward him like a meteor, Jin Taekyung opened his eyes wide. He was still buried deep in the ground.

[P153]
Crunch.

[P154]
Solid earth crumbled like mud beneath her strike. Jin Taekyung escaped it by a hair and flicked his sleeve.

[P155]
A dagger flew at her from somewhere, as though he had conjured it from thin air. She avoided it easily and thrust out her hand with lightning speed.

[P156]
Slash!

[P157]
Her fingers only grazed him.

[P158]
But curled like hooks, they tore through his martial uniform and cut into his thigh.

[P159]
Blood spurted. Jin Taekyung staggered.

[P160]
The Southern Heaven Demon Empress beamed as she brought the edge of her hand down toward him.

[P161]
Whoooosh!

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). **Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.

Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.
